SCREENING V0.1

A working prototype, with explicit assumptions.

This version uses a transparent weighted score. It has not been trained or validated on Indian sewer outcomes. All 12 built-in records are fabricated. Chennai locality names provide context only; no CMWSSB asset or incident data is represented.

Source files, cleaning rules & missing inputs

How the score works

Score = the rounded sum of each factor’s weight × its normalised risk value. Normalised values are capped between 0 and 1. Weights and thresholds below are project assumptions, not calibrated standards.

Low · 0–34Moderate · 35–64High · 65–100
FACTORMAX POINTSNORMALISATION

Material multipliers: PVC/HDPE 0.15; concrete 0.55; vitrified clay 0.80; cast iron 0.70; brick 0.90; unknown 0.50; source labels SW Pipe 0.80, DI Pipe 0.50, DWC Pipe 0.30, PSC Pipe 0.60, MS Pipe 0.65. These illustrative values ignore construction quality, slope and condition. Unknown material is flagged in the result.

Practical Indian-city data workflow

  1. Start with sample scenarios

    Download the CSV and test the workflow. Keep data_source as “Synthetic sample” for fabricated inputs.

  2. Request asset and incident logs

    Ask CMWSSB for pipe IDs, material, diameter, installation dates, cleaning dates, and dated blockage incidents. Public sewer geometry and coded dimensions are available; this build has not verified downloadable asset-level blockage and cleaning histories.

  3. Add a public rainfall source

    IMD daily gridded rainfall archive provides a possible rainfall input. Extract the grid near the asset, sum the 7 days before the assessment date, and record source, date and resolution. A 0.25° grid is coarse for pipe-level analysis.

  4. Keep complaints and outcomes separate

    Government sewer complaint service is a reporting channel, not proof of an open historical dataset. Deduplicate available complaints and verify sewer links. Surface flooding alone does not establish sewer blockage.

  5. Join, label and then train

    Join by asset/ward and dates. Build inputs only from information available at prediction time. For a future ML model, define “verified blockage within 30 days”, include observed non-events, split by time and location, and evaluate calibration, PR-AUC and recall against a simple baseline.

The Chennai explorer above includes a bundled public-data snapshot. It does not refresh automatically. Missing municipal data must stay missing or be explicitly marked as estimated; never manufacture real observations.

CSV guide & prototype limits

One row per sewer assessment

All columns and numeric fields are required. Use YYYY-MM-DD dates, millimetres for rainfall and diameter, and people/sites per km² for density. Zero means a measured or deliberately assumed zero, not “unknown”. Only material accepts “Unknown”. Mixed public and estimated inputs must use “Mixed / estimated” and explain which fields were estimated.

Uploads replace the current dataset after every row passes validation. Maximum 1,000 records and 2 MB. Duplicate IDs, missing values and out-of-range numbers are rejected.

Your records stay in this session

CSV files are parsed in your browser and are not sent to a prediction server. No records are saved between visits. Export results before refreshing or closing the page. Exported CSV files include provenance and model version.

The cleaning scenario resets cleaning delay to zero and assumes at least four cleanings per year. It only recomputes two assumed factors; it is not evidence of treatment effectiveness.

No claim of model accuracy, confidence percentage, inspection status, hydraulic capacity or structural safety is made. Real maintenance decisions need verified records and engineering review.
